constraints: Billing only through the app stores (no direct card billing at launch)
No sales or support team; everything must be self-serve
The free tier must remain genuinely useful — it is the growth engine
Server costs scale with sync and storage usage, so heavy users cost real money

options.label: Flat $5/month (or $50/year)
options.summary: One premium tier, everything included, monthly or annual billing.

options.label: $3/month base plus paid add-on packs
options.summary: Cheap entry tier; power features (extra storage, automation, exports) sold as add-on packs.

options.label: Annual-only at $40/year
options.summary: No monthly option; one annual plan, everything included.

question: A free consumer notes-and-lists app with about 120,000 monthly users is launching a premium tier. Should it price flat, price cheap with add-ons, or go annual-only?
stakes: Pricing set at launch is sticky: early subscribers anchor expectations, and migrating a large base between pricing structures later is painful and churn-heavy.
